report.releaseDate: 19 Nov 2026 (ADG September 2026 Event Wagering & Fantasy Sports figures; 9M-26 roll-up published 25 Nov 2026)
report.verdict: Arizona is a ~$9bn-handle, mobile-only-in-practice sports-betting market growing at low single digits (9M-26 handle $6.54bn, +3% YoY) with the cheapest fiscal terms of any large US state — 10% on receipts net of promos, an effective ~6–7% of gross win. The two things that matter for an entrant are (i) access, because the 20-licence cap means you need a tribal or pro-team partner, and (ii) tax risk, because the Governor's 45% large-operator proposal is unenacted but not dead. No online casino, and none coming without a compact rewrite.

summary: **Market size — handle, not revenue, is the headline:** Arizona bettors staked $6.54bn in 9M 2026, +3% YoY (Gaming Intelligence roll-up of ADG monthly reports). Our own sum of the nine ADG monthly releases is ≈$6.58bn (Jan $881.1m, Feb $760.4m, Mar $836.9m, Apr $737.2m, May $676.7m, Jun $663.9m, Jul $599.5m, Aug $582.8m, Sep $836.7m); the ~$35m gap likely reflects post-release revisions and is flagged.

**Growth has stalled on a like-for-like basis:** H1-26 handle was $4.56bn (+2%); Q3-26 ≈$2.02bn with Jul +29.3%, Aug -5% and Sep -1.7% YoY. March (-5.7%) and April (-1.2%) also fell. The +3% 9M print is flattered by July's weak 2025 comparator; underlying volume is flat-to-slightly-up in a maturing fifth-year market.

**Fiscal year lens (ADG FY2026 Annual Report):** total gross event-wagering receipts (wagers) of $9,077,458,841 for Jul-25–Jun-26, generating $57,757,546 of event-wagering privilege fees; event wagering plus fantasy contributed $61,078,501 in privilege and licensing fees. Implied taxable AGR ≈$578m for the fiscal year (fees ÷ ~10%), i.e. a 6.4% taxable hold on handle.

**Revenue is the volatile line:** disclosed taxable adjusted gross event-wagering receipts (AGR after promo deductions) ran $40.7m (Feb), $47.6m (Mar), $59.8m (Apr, +37.8% YoY), $47.6m (May), $30.7m (Jun, -39% YoY vs $50.5m), $48.6m (Jul) and $33.0m (Sep). Seven disclosed months total $308.0m taxable AGR and $30.6m fees; January and August revenue lines were not retrievable from a primary source (n/a). Gross hold swung from 7.8% (Sep) to 11.0% (Jul); taxable hold from 3.9% (Sep) to 8.1% (Apr/Jul).

**Promotional deductions are the key leakage:** operators deducted $32.2m of free bets/promo credits in September against $65.2m gross win (49%), $21.7m vs $52.4m in June (41%), $17.0m vs $65.7m in July (26%) and $18.7m vs $66.3m in May (28%). On handle, deductions run 2.8–3.9%, far inside the statutory cap, so the cap is non-binding and the state's effective take on gross win is only ~6–7%.

**Online penetration is effectively total:** mobile was $833.9m of $836.7m in September (99.7%), $581.2m of $582.8m in August and $734.4m of $737.2m in April; retail (tribal casino sportsbooks, pro-venue books and limited OTB/track licensees) handles $1.6–2.8m a month and is taxed at 8% rather than 10%.

**Concentration — a two-horse market:** September mobile handle: FanDuel $270.8m (32.5%), DraftKings $242.0m (29.0%), BetMGM $77.3m (9.3%); August: FanDuel $186.4m (32.1%), DraftKings $163.4m (28.1%), Fanatics $71.0m (12.2%). FanDuel + DraftKings = 61% of September handle; Caesars and bet365 round out the top six (April). Sporttrade exited in 2026; Circa Sports Arizona (designee of the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe) was allocated a licence in August 2026.

**Licensing regime — capped and partner-gated:** A.R.S. Title 5, Ch.10 (HB 2772, 2021; launch 9 Sep 2021) allows up to 20 event-wagering operator licences — 10 reserved for compact tribes and 10 for professional sports franchises/facility owners — plus 10 limited (in-person only) licences for racetracks/OTB sites. ADG's website listed 15 event-wagering licensees in Sep-26, three not yet launched. Fees: $100,000 application, $750,000 initial licence, $150,000 annual renewal (licence term not verified). A new application window ran 26 Jun–10 Jul 2026.

**Tax regime — 'privilege fee' on net receipts:** 10% of adjusted gross event-wagering receipts for mobile, 8% for retail; base is wagers less winnings, federal excise (0.25% of handle) and allowable free-bet/promo deductions. Fantasy contests pay 5% of adjusted revenue. Arizona's 10% headline is the fifth-lowest sportsbook rate in the US (iGB).

**Tax change risk — the 45% proposal:** Governor Hobbs's FY2027 executive budget (Jan/Feb 2026) proposed raising the privilege fee to 45% for 'large operators' taking ≥$75m handle per month. It was not enacted; all operators still pay 10% as of Nov-26. On September data, a 45% rate on the FanDuel/DraftKings share (~61% of taxable AGR) would have lifted state fees from $3.3m to roughly $10.4m (illustrative estimate) — a 3x take with no change in player economics, and BetMGM/Fanatics hover around the threshold.

**Fantasy sports is small but growing in the pick'em era:** September entry fees $13.6m, adjusted revenue $2.2m, fees $111,221; PrizePicks led with $1.12m adjusted revenue, DraftKings $544k. FY2026 fantasy adjusted revenue was $26.6m (≈$1.3m fees at 5%).

**Prediction markets are being prosecuted, not licensed:** Arizona filed 20 criminal counts against Kalshi in 2026 alleging unlawful acceptance of bets on political contests, college sports and individual player performances. This is the most aggressive state posture in the US and signals that ADG/AG will defend the licensed channel — and tribal exclusivity — against event-contract substitutes.

**No online casino, and no near-term path:** Arizona authorises only sports/event wagering (mobile + retail), fantasy, tribal Class III casinos under the 2021 amended compact, the state lottery and pari-mutuel racing. iGaming would require compact renegotiation with 16+ tribes; no bill advanced in the 2026 session [unverified].

**Payments and RG are standard US-regulated:** 21+ with KYC and in-state geolocation; ADG runs the statewide self-exclusion list and the Division of Problem Gambling (1-800-NEXT-STEP); operators must offer deposit/time limits and carry RG messaging in advertising. Payment rails are card/ACH/e-wallet/Play+ and cage cash; mobile-money is not a feature of this market. Credit-card deposit permissibility not verified.

**Enforcement direction of travel:** ADG issued cease-and-desist actions against unlicensed offshore and sweepstakes operators through 2025 and escalated to criminal charges against Kalshi in 2026; ADG also allocated a new tribal-designee licence (Circa) rather than expanding the cap — the regulator protects the channel but does not widen it.

**Cumulative scale and fiscal contribution:** since launch, ~$38bn wagered and $205.4m of privilege fees (0.54% of handle). FY2027 to date (June–September activity) EW fees are $14.8m plus $349,935 fantasy.

**Read-through for B2Tech:** this is a large, cheap-to-tax, single-product market in which the top two hold >60% and promo intensity is ~3–4% of handle; organic entry is impossible without a tribal or pro-team licence partner (or acquiring an exiting designee), and the realistic upside is a 3–6% share niche (BetMGM/Fanatics territory, ~$75–100m monthly handle) at ~7–9% gross hold. The decision hinges on partner availability and the probability the 45% tier returns in the 2027 budget cycle.

segments.name: Sports betting — mobile (99.7% of the market)
segments.headline: A $9bn-handle market that has stopped growing in volume, where hold and promo intensity — not stakes — decide revenue and tax.
narrative: Volume has plateaued. Handle of $6.54bn for 9M 2026 is +3% on 9M 2025 (implied ≈$6.35bn), but the monthly profile shows a market that is flat on a like-for-like basis: January ($881.1m) was the high, August ($582.8m) the low, and the three most comparable football/basketball months — March (-5.7%), April (-1.2%) and September (-1.7%) — all fell year on year. July's +29.3% and June's +22.3% came against soft 2025 comparators (≈$464m and ≈$543m). Q3-26 handle was ≈$2.02bn; Q4 seasonality (October 2025 was the record month, November 2025 $965.2m) implies a CY2026 handle of roughly $9.3–9.6bn (our estimate, not a reported figure).

Revenue is a hold story. Gross win (adjusted gross receipts before promo deductions) ran $66.3m in May (9.8% hold), $52.4m in June (7.9%), $65.7m in July (11.0%) and $65.2m in September (7.8%); taxable AGR after promo deductions was $47.6m, $30.7m, $48.6m and $33.0m respectively. April was the best month of the period with $59.8m taxable AGR (+37.8% YoY, 8.1% taxable hold) on a lower handle, while June's taxable AGR fell 39% YoY to $30.7m despite handle +22%. For a new entrant the planning assumptions are a 7–9% gross hold with a ±2pt monthly standard deviation and promo deductions of 3–4% of handle.

Promotional spend is heavy and fully deductible in practice. September's $32.2m of free bets and promotional credits equalled 49% of gross win and 3.85% of handle; June's $21.7m was 41% of gross win. Because the statutory cap is expressed against gross receipts (stakes) rather than win, it never binds, and the state's effective take on gross win is ~5–7% rather than the 10% headline. That is both the attraction of the market and the reason the Governor targeted the large operators' rate.

Share is concentrated and sticky. FanDuel ($270.8m, 32.5% of September mobile handle) and DraftKings ($242.0m, 29.0%) together took 61% of all stakes; BetMGM ($77.3m, 9.3%) and Fanatics ($71.0m, 12.2% in August) alternate as the third brand, with Caesars and bet365 completing the top six. The tail — Hard Rock Bet, Desert Diamond Sports (Tohono O'odham), Betfred and betPARX [presence as at Sep-26 unverified] — shares the remaining ~15–20%. Sporttrade's 2026 exit shows that sub-scale exchange/novel models do not clear the fixed cost of a $750k licence plus $150k renewals and partner revenue shares; Circa's August 2026 licence allocation through the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe shows the opposite path still works for a differentiated book.

Product and rules. Arizona permits in-play and pre-match betting on professional, collegiate and selected other events; political contests are prohibited and the Kalshi complaint frames certain college and individual-player markets as unlawful, so an entrant should assume constraints on college props [exact scope unverified]. Mobile wagering requires in-state geolocation; tribal designees operate under the amended 2021 compact. The economics that matter for B2Tech: a 5% share of a $9.5bn market is ≈$475m handle, ≈$35–40m gross win and ≈$22–27m taxable AGR a year before marketing — viable only with a partner structure that keeps revenue share below the state's own 10%.

segments.name: Sports betting — retail, limited event wagering & fantasy contests
segments.headline: Retail is a rounding error ($1.6–2.8m a month) taxed at 8%; fantasy is a $27m-adjusted-revenue niche led by PrizePicks.
narrative: Retail event wagering — sportsbooks inside tribal casinos, pro-sports venues (Chase Field, Footprint Center, State Farm Stadium area) and the up-to-10 limited event-wagering licensees at racetracks and OTB sites — handled $2.8m in September, $1.6m in August and $2.8m in April, i.e. 0.2–0.4% of stakes. The 8% retail privilege fee versus 10% mobile is immaterial at this scale. For an operator, retail matters only as a brand-activation and cage-cash deposit channel attached to a partner's venue, not as a P&L line.

Fantasy sports contests (A.R.S. Title 5, Ch.11) are taxed at 5% of adjusted revenue. September 2026 in-state entry fees were $13.6m, adjusted revenue $2.2m and fees $111,221; July was $8.0m / $1.5m / $74,058 and June $9.3m / $1.7m / $86,860. PrizePicks reported the largest September adjusted revenue ($1.12m) ahead of DraftKings ($544k), confirming that pick'em-style contests dominate. FY2026 fantasy adjusted revenue was $26.6m (≈$1.3m fees), roughly 4–5% of the sportsbook taxable AGR base.

The fantasy line is strategically relevant because it is the lightly-taxed adjacent product that national operators use for acquisition; Arizona's regulator reports it monthly alongside event wagering and has not moved against pick'em formats, in contrast with several other states. An entrant without a sportsbook licence could still operate fantasy contests under the separate fantasy licence, but the economics are small.

Cumulative context: since 9 September 2021 Arizona has taken ~$38bn in sports wagers and remitted $205.4m in event-wagering privilege fees; FY2027 to date (June–September activity) is $14.8m from event wagering and $349,935 from fantasy, ahead of the FY2026 pace on a like-for-like basis only because of July's strong hold.

segments.name: Licensing, market access & tax regime
segments.headline: Twenty full licences, each tied to a tribe or a pro franchise; 10%/8% on receipts net of promos today, with a 45% large-operator tier proposed but unenacted.
narrative: Legal framework. HB 2772 (signed April 2021) created A.R.S. Title 5, Chapter 10 (event wagering) and Chapter 11 (fantasy sports) and was paired with amended Tribal-State Gaming Compacts; the Arizona Department of Gaming (ADG), through its Event Wagering & Fantasy Sports division, is the licensing, rule-making and enforcement body, and also regulates tribal gaming compliance, racing and unarmed combat. Wagering went live on 9 September 2021.

Licence architecture. Up to 20 event-wagering operator licences: 10 reserved for federally recognised Arizona tribes with a compact and 10 for owners of professional sports franchises or facilities (NFL, MLB, NBA, NHL, WNBA/MLS-class teams, PGA Tour host venue, NASCAR track). Each licensee may run one retail book and one online skin via a designated operator/management-services provider, which is why national brands appear as designees of tribes or teams. A further 10 limited event-wagering licences allow in-person only wagering at racetracks and OTB sites. ADG listed 15 event-wagering licensees in September 2026 (three not yet launched), opened an application window from 26 June to 10 July 2026 and allocated a licence to Circa Sports Arizona LLC (designee of the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe) in August 2026 — confirming that tribal slots remain the live entry route. Fees are $100,000 (application), $750,000 (initial licence) and $150,000 (annual renewal); licence term and management-services-provider fees were not verified from a primary source.

Tax regime. Operators pay a 'privilege fee' on adjusted gross event-wagering receipts — stakes less winnings paid, federal excise tax and allowable free-bet/promotional credits — at 10% for mobile and 8% for retail; fantasy contests pay 5% of adjusted revenue. Because promo deductions run 26–49% of gross win, the effective rate on gross win is ~5–7%, which with the 10% headline (fifth-lowest in the US) makes Arizona the most operator-friendly large state after Nevada and Iowa. FY2026 fees were $57.76m on $9.08bn handle (0.64%); the step-down schedule for promo deductions in statute could not be verified and is flagged.

Pending change. Governor Hobbs's FY2027 executive budget proposed a 45% privilege fee for 'large operators' handling at least $75m a month — in practice FanDuel and DraftKings every month, and BetMGM/Fanatics in peak months. The Republican-controlled Legislature did not adopt it and the 10% rate remains in force as of November 2026. Applied to September 2026, our illustrative estimate is that state fees would have risen from $3.3m to ~$10.4m; the more probable 2027 compromise, in our view, is a narrower change (a mid-teens flat rate or restriction of promo deductibility) rather than 45%, but the proposal establishes a political anchor that did not exist before. Tribal partners also have a stake: a tiered tax that hits designees changes the revenue-share arithmetic under existing agreements.

Implication for an entrant. Access is binary: without a tribe or franchise willing to designate you (or purchase of an exiting designee's position), there is no path. Fixed costs are modest ($1m year one, $150k thereafter plus partner share), but share is hard to win against a 61% duopoly spending ~3–4% of handle on promos. Price the tax at 10% today but stress-test at 20–45% on any handle above $75m a month.

segments.name: Adjacent verticals, payments, responsible gambling & enforcement
segments.headline: No iGaming and no lottery-online casino; tribal exclusivity shapes everything, and the state is prosecuting prediction markets rather than accommodating them.
narrative: Product perimeter. Arizona's regulated gambling comprises tribal Class III casinos (slots, table games under the 2021 amended compact, which also expanded tribal gaming in exchange for sports betting), state-wide mobile and retail sports/event wagering, fantasy contests, the Arizona Lottery and pari-mutuel horse racing with OTB. Online casino and online poker are not authorised; because tribal exclusivity over casino-style gaming is compact-protected, iGaming would require renegotiation with the 16-plus gaming tribes and there is no live legislative vehicle [2026 session status unverified]. Tribal casino GGR is not published by ADG at facility level; tribal contributions to the state's Arizona Benefits Fund are reported in the ADG annual report but were not retrieved here (n/a).

Prediction markets. Arizona filed criminal charges against Kalshi in 2026 — 20 counts alleging unlawful acceptance of bets on political contests, college sports and individual player performances. Combined with ADG's 2025 cease-and-desist campaign against offshore and sweepstakes operators, the enforcement posture is the most assertive of any US state and protects licensed operators' addressable market; the counter-risk is that a federal pre-emption ruling in Kalshi's favour would open an untaxed 0%-privilege-fee channel for event contracts.

Payments. Deposits and withdrawals run on standard US regulated rails — debit cards, ACH/online banking, PayPal and similar e-wallets, Play+ prepaid, and cash at partner casino cages; there is no mobile-money dimension. Whether credit-card deposits are permitted under ADG rules was not verified. Geolocation (in-state) and KYC at 21+ are mandatory. Withdrawal speed and cage access are competitive differentiators for tribal-partnered brands (Desert Diamond, BetMGM/Gila River).

Responsible gambling and advertising. ADG operates a statewide self-exclusion programme covering event wagering and fantasy and funds problem-gambling services (1-800-NEXT-STEP) partly from privilege fees; operators must offer deposit, wager and time limits, display RG messaging and avoid advertising aimed at under-21s. Arizona has not followed Ohio/Massachusetts in banning 'risk-free' language by statute or restricting college-athlete marketing by rule as far as we could verify; the Kalshi complaint's reference to individual player performance markets suggests scope limits on props exist in the event-catalogue rules [unverified].

Enforcement and political direction. The regulator is expanding supply only through the statutory tribal slots (Circa), prosecuting unlicensed substitutes, and publishing monthly operator-level data; the executive branch wants a far larger fiscal share from the two national leaders. The direction is therefore 'protect the channel, tax it harder', not liberalise — which favours incumbents' volumes but threatens their margins.

blocks.heading: Product perimeter
blocks.takeaway: No iGaming or online poker; tribal exclusivity under the 2021 compact means iGaming would need renegotiation with 16-plus tribes.
points: Regulated gambling: tribal Class III casinos, mobile/retail event wagering, fantasy, Arizona Lottery, pari-mutuel racing with OTB.
2021 amended compact expanded tribal gaming in exchange for sports betting.
No live legislative vehicle for iGaming [2026 session status unverified].
Tribal casino GGR not published at facility level; Arizona Benefits Fund contributions in ADG annual report not retrieved (n/a).

blocks.heading: Prediction markets
blocks.takeaway: Arizona filed 20 criminal counts against Kalshi in 2026, the most assertive enforcement posture of any US state.
points: Counts allege unlawful bets on political contests, college sports and individual player performances.
Combined with ADG's 2025 cease-and-desist campaign against offshore and sweepstakes operators, this protects licensed operators' addressable market.
Counter-risk: a federal pre-emption ruling for Kalshi would open an untaxed 0%-privilege-fee channel for event contracts.

blocks.heading: Payments
blocks.takeaway: Deposits run on standard US regulated rails with mandatory in-state geolocation and 21+ KYC; no mobile-money dimension.
points: Rails: debit cards, ACH/online banking, PayPal and similar e-wallets, Play+ prepaid, cash at partner casino cages.
Credit-card deposit permission under ADG rules not verified.
Withdrawal speed and cage access are differentiators for tribal-partnered brands (Desert Diamond, BetMGM/Gila River).

blocks.heading: Responsible gambling
blocks.takeaway: ADG runs statewide self-exclusion and funds 1-800-NEXT-STEP partly from privilege fees; no statutory 'risk-free' ad ban verified.
points: Operators must offer deposit, wager and time limits, display RG messaging and avoid advertising aimed at under-21s.
Arizona has not followed Ohio/Massachusetts on 'risk-free' language or college-athlete marketing restrictions as far as verified.
Kalshi complaint suggests scope limits on individual player props exist in event-catalogue rules [unverified].

blocks.heading: Political direction
blocks.takeaway: Direction is 'protect the channel, tax it harder', not liberalise — favouring incumbents' volumes but threatening their margins.
points: Regulator expands supply only via statutory tribal slots (Circa), prosecutes unlicensed substitutes and publishes monthly operator-level data.
Executive branch wants a far larger fiscal share from the two national leaders.

highlights.text: Lowest effective tax among large states: 10% mobile / 8% retail on receipts net of promos, equating to ~5–7% of gross win in 2026 months; FY2026 fees were only 0.64% of $9.08bn handle.
Scale and maturity: ~$9bn annual handle, fifth-/sixth-largest US state by monthly handle, 99.7% mobile, monthly operator-level transparency from ADG — a market that can be modelled precisely.

Access route still open: tribal licence slots remain available (Circa allocated via the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe in Aug-26; application window Jun–Jul 2026) and Sporttrade's exit frees a designee position; entry cost is ~$1m year one plus $150k p.a.
Hold tailwind: gross hold of 7.8–11.0% in disclosed 2026 months and April taxable AGR +37.8% YoY show parlay/SGP mix lifting revenue even as handle flattens.
Regulator defends the licensed channel: criminal charges against Kalshi and C&Ds against offshore/sweepstakes operators reduce leakage to untaxed substitutes.
Fantasy pick'em is tolerated at a 5% fee ($13.6m entry fees in Sep-26; PrizePicks leads), giving a low-cost acquisition adjacency not available in several other states.

lowlights.text: Tax-hike overhang: the Governor's 45% tier for operators with ≥$75m monthly handle was not enacted in 2026 but will likely return in the January 2027 budget; our illustrative estimate is a 3x state take on September data if applied.
Duopoly: FanDuel + DraftKings hold 61% of handle; the third slot rotates between BetMGM and Fanatics at ~9–12%, leaving a long tail fighting over ~15–20% with promo intensity of 3–4% of handle.
Volume growth has stalled: March -5.7%, April -1.2%, August -5%, September -1.7% YoY; the +3% 9M print rests on weak mid-2025 comparators.
Revenue volatility: taxable AGR swung from $59.8m (Apr) to $30.7m (Jun) and $33.0m (Sep) — June -39% YoY on +22% handle — so monthly cash flow and fee remittances are hold-driven and lumpy.
Licence-cap lock-in: 20 full licences tied to tribes/teams means no organic entry and dependence on partner revenue shares that can exceed the state's own 10% take.
No iGaming and no realistic path: tribal compact exclusivity rules out online casino, capping the cross-sell upside that justifies US entry elsewhere.

Data reliance: ADG's monthly reports are operator self-reported and unaudited; our 9M figures rely on secondary reproductions because the ADG site was unreachable, and the GI 9M handle ($6.54bn) differs from the sum of monthly releases (≈$6.58bn).

forecast.intro: Nothing in the rulebook changed in 9M 2026 — rate still 10%/8%, cap still 20 licences, promos still fully deductible in practice — but the political and competitive bridges moved. The Governor put a 45% large-operator tier on the table; the Legislature rejected it; ADG added supply only via the tribal route (Circa) while Sporttrade left; and the state turned prediction markets into a criminal matter. The fiscal bridge below applies the proposal to September 2026 to size what is at stake for the two leaders and, by extension, any partner-dependent entrant.

bridge.title: Sep-26 privilege fees — current regime (10% mobile / 8% retail)
Uplift if 45% applied to ≥$75m/month operators (FanDuel + DraftKings ≈61% of taxable AGR, est.)

forecast.view: Our independent view: **CY2026 handle lands at ~$9.3–9.6bn (estimate), +2–4%**, with Q4 carrying the year on NFL/NBA seasonality; **taxable AGR runs ~$575–625m annualised** (FY2026 implied $578m) at a 6–6.5% taxable hold, and state fees ~$58–63m. Volume growth in 2027 is low-single-digit at best; revenue growth depends on parlay mix. On rules, we assign **a low probability (≈20–25%) that a 45% tier is enacted in the 2027 session** given legislative control and tribal-compact entanglement, but **a materially higher probability (≈40–50%) of some fiscal tightening** — a flat 15–20% rate or a cap/phase-out of promo deductibility — because the executive has now anchored the debate and neighbouring states (Illinois, New Jersey, Maryland, Louisiana) have raised rates. Supply will stay capped; expect one or two further tribal-designee allocations and at least one more small-brand exit. Online casino: no change before 2028 at the earliest. Prediction-market litigation is the swing factor: a Kalshi win on pre-emption would create an untaxed substitute and strengthen the case for lower, not higher, sportsbook taxes; a state win entrenches the licensed channel.
watch: January 2027 executive budget (FY2028): whether the 45% ≥$75m tier returns, is replaced by a flat increase, or targets promo deductibility; and the Legislature's budget negotiations through June 2027.
Kalshi criminal case and parallel federal pre-emption litigation — outcome, timing, and whether ADG extends enforcement to other event-contract venues.
ADG licence allocations: timing of Circa Sports Arizona launch, use of remaining tribal slots, any further designee exits/transfers, and whether ADG opens another application window in 2027.

October–December 2026 monthly reports: October 2025 was the record handle month; a YoY decline in Q4 would confirm volume saturation, while taxable hold above 6.5% would confirm the parlay-mix thesis.
Promo deductions as a share of gross win (49% in Sep-26): sustained >40% would make deductibility the easiest political target.
Any iGaming or compact-amendment discussion between the Governor's office and tribes, and NCAA/college-prop restrictions in ADG event-catalogue rulemaking.

report.confidenceNote: Market reports in USD; no FX conversion required. The ADG website (monthly Event Wagering Revenue Reports, 19-Nov-2026 press release) was unreachable during research, so monthly handle/AGR/fee figures were taken from secondary reproductions of ADG releases (Gaming Intelligence, iGB, betarizona, rg.org, Fox10, Casino City Times/Indian Gaming reprints of the ADG press release) and cross-checked where two sources overlapped (Sep-26: iGB vs Joe Wager; Apr-26: rg.org vs Indian Gaming vs betarizona; FY2026: ADG Annual Report excerpt). Unverified/derived items: January 2026 and August 2026 gross win, taxable AGR and fees (August ≈$3.6m fee and ≈$36m taxable AGR derived from FY2027 YTD and cumulative totals); 9M taxable AGR and fee estimates; the statutory promo-deduction step-down schedule; licence term and MSP fees; credit-card deposit rules; 2026 iGaming bill status; presence of tail brands (Hard Rock, Desert Diamond, Betfred, betPARX) as at Sep-26. The GI 9M handle ($6.54bn) differs from the sum of ADG monthly releases (≈$6.58bn); the GI figure is used as headline and the gap flagged. All forward figures and the 45% pro-forma are our estimates, not reported data.
